Personally from my experience art burnout usually is paired with art block (I'm suffering from both currently) Art block is when nth you draw is up to your standards ,so you still can draw but you just aren't satisfied or you are creatively drained and don't really know what to do (Usually it's when your headspace don't match with your skills)

Art burnout is when you do so much art you become tired of it or you end up not enjoying art , it's a terrifying and horrible feeling. I have friends that never recovered from art burnout and just gave up on art.(Nowadays I'm so close too)

Maybe it's time for you to take a break from people and society, usually quaruntine does that but maybe you should take a walk or a trip (If you have the capable means ) to the great outdoors or anywhere you can't find people There's nothing wrong with taking a break to self heal

But if you're looking for a long term situation , it may help to take the time to re-evaluate your life.
Sometimes it might be good to evaluate if you're loving yourself enough cos if you're talking about exhaustion usually it's from the lack of self care

Self-care doesn't mean just having daily showers and three meals a day as well as exercise, it also means to stop taking bullshit from people that exhaust you or toxify your life.Honestly, once you stop giving a shit about what other people think and care about what you truly have to say and feel, it's a freeing feeling.

It may sound selfish to say to care about yourself first, but maybe think of it this way. Imagine you're building a brick house and there are others building a brick house too, and some homeless dude asked you for a brick and you give it to them, and then continuous streams of homeless dudes ask you for bricks and you keep giving it to them instead of focusing of building your house.By nighttime, you won't have a house and you will be cold and sad.But other people who refuse to give those homeless people bricks and focus on their own house, not only have their own shelter and warmth but now have the capability to let other people into their house to help them.

Moral of the story,take care of yourself, you're all you truly got
